title: The Sabbatical Year

questions.question: At the end of every seven years, what must happen?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:1 (ESV): "At the end of every seven years you shall grant a release."

questions.question: What is the nature of the release?
options: Every creditor shall release what he has lent to his neighbor
questions.correctAnswer: Every creditor shall release what he has lent to his neighbor
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:2 (ESV): "...Every creditor shall release what he has lent to his neighbor. He shall not exact it..."

questions.question: Should you give to the poor brother?
options: Yes, freely and without a grudging heart
questions.correctAnswer: Yes, freely and without a grudging heart
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:10 (ESV): "You shall give to him freely, and your heart shall not be grudging when you give to him..."

questions.question: If a Hebrew slave has served six years, what happens in the seventh?
options: You shall let him go free
questions.correctAnswer: You shall let him go free
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:12 (ESV): "...he shall serve you six years, and in the seventh year you shall let him go free from you."

questions.question: When letting a slave go, how should they be sent?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:13–14 (ESV): "And when you let him go free... you shall not let him go empty-handed. You shall furnish him liberally..."

questions.question: Why should there be no poor among them?
options: Because the Lord will bless them if they obey
questions.correctAnswer: Because the Lord will bless them if they obey
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:4 (ESV): "But there will be no poor among you; for the Lord will bless you..."

questions.question: What if a slave says "I love you and your house" and will not leave?
options: Pierce his ear with an awl to the door; he is a servant forever
questions.correctAnswer: Pierce his ear with an awl to the door; he is a servant forever
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:16–17 (ESV): "...then you shall take an awl, and put it through his ear into the door, and he shall be your bondservant forever."

questions.question: What evil thought might one have regarding the seventh year?
options: "The seventh year, the year of release is near," so be stingy
questions.correctAnswer: "The seventh year, the year of release is near," so be stingy
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:9 (ESV): "Take care lest there be an unworthy thought in your heart and you say, 'The seventh year, the year of release is near,' and your eye look grudgingly..."

questions.question: Who may be pressed for repayment during the release?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:3 (ESV): "Of a foreigner you may exact it, but whatever of yours is with your brother your hand shall release."

questions.question: What concerning the firstborn males of the herd and flock?
options: Dedicate to the Lord; do no work with them
questions.correctAnswer: Dedicate to the Lord; do no work with them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:19 (ESV): "All the firstborn males... you shall dedicate to the Lord... You shall do no work with the firstborn of your ox..."

questions.question: Why will the poor never cease out of the land?
options: Implied result of disobedience or simple reality
questions.correctAnswer: Implied result of disobedience or simple reality
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:11 (ESV): "For the poor will never cease to be out of the land. Therefore I command you..."

questions.question: If a firstborn animal has a blemish (lame or blind), what then?
options: You shall not sacrifice it; eat it in your towns
questions.correctAnswer: You shall not sacrifice it; eat it in your towns
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:21–22 (ESV): "But if it has any blemish... you shall not sacrifice it... You shall eat it within your towns..."

questions.question: From what sources should you furnish the freed slave?
options: Out of the flock, threshing floor, and winepress
questions.correctAnswer: Out of the flock, threshing floor, and winepress
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:14 (ESV): "...out of your flock, out of your threshing floor, and out of your winepress."

questions.question: A servant serves for six years worth how much of a hired worker?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:18 (ESV): "...for at half the cost of a hired worker he has served you six years."

questions.question: Why should they remember Egypy regarding slaves?
options: God redeemed them from house of slavery
questions.correctAnswer: God redeemed them from house of slavery
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 15:15 (ESV): "You shall remember that you were a slave... and the Lord your God redeemed you..."

key_verse_text: For the poor will never cease to be out of the land. Therefore I command you, “You shall open wide your hand to your brother, to the needy and to the poor, in your land.” (ESV)
